solutionSteps.instruction: Take the square root of both sides, keeping both signs.

contentBlocks.value: the square root of (x − 4)² is x − 4

strategyBlocks.value: Take the square root of both sides, remembering the ±, then add 4.

whyThisWorks.value: A squared bracket equal to a positive number gives two solutions because both √13 and −√13 square to 13. The two roots sit an equal distance either side of x = 4, which is the axis of symmetry of the parabola y = (x − 4)². Expanding first would only undo the convenient form you have been handed.

commonErrors.misconception: Expanding to x² − 8x + 16 = 13 and doing unnecessary work.
